description: Matched-pair constant-time RTL fixtures. Every constant-time design ships beside a deliberately leaky twin with an identical module interface, so a tool is graded against controls rather than against itself.
observation_semantics: A design is CONSTANT_TIME with respect to `observation` when the cycle at which `observation` asserts is independent of every signal listed in `secrets`. A tool must return CONSTANT_TIME or LEAKY for each scored fixture.

scored.note: Barrett modular reduction with a data-oblivious cycle counter.
Completion is skipped when the conditional-subtract is not taken, so timing reveals a magnitude comparison.

OUT-OF-REMIT CONTROL. Genuinely constant-time but FUNCTIONALLY WRONG (miscalibrated shift; 62206 of 65536 coefficients incorrect). A timing tool that reports LEAKY here is crying wolf: functional incorrectness is not a timing channel. This fixture separates serious tools from pattern-matchers.
Tag comparison that always scans all W bits (the memcmp-hardening pattern).
Early-exit memcmp: completion timing reveals the first-mismatch position.
Restoring divider that always runs the full width.
Identical to ct_div_wide except completion also fires on an early exit when the remainder is exhausted.
Binary GCD run for a fixed operand-independent iteration count.
Textbook Euclid: the number of reduction steps, hence the cycle at which done asserts, depends on the operands.
The leaky twin after repair; a tool that flags this has not distinguished the fix from the defect.
Shift-and-add multiplier that skips cycles on zero multiplier bits.
Montgomery-ladder style exponentiation: both branches always execute.
Square-and-multiply: the multiply is skipped on a zero exponent bit, leaking the exponent Hamming weight.

unscored.reason: Combinational reference model with no completion signal; used as the functional oracle for the barrett pair, not as a timing fixture.
Fault-detection fixture. Its observable is a data output, which must depend on the operands; grading it under the constant-time task would be a category error.
Fault-detection fixture (single-bit parity variant), as above.
Secret-residue fixture: the property of interest is whether operand state survives completion, not completion timing. Reserved for a future `secret_residue` task.
Secret-residue fixture (operand registers cleared on completion). Reserved for the `secret_residue` task.
Secret-residue fixture (only some operand registers cleared) — the discriminating twin. Reserved for the `secret_residue` task.
Secret-residue fixture. Reserved for the `secret_residue` task.
Simulation testbench, not a design under test.
